prTitle: fix(app-web-sdk): resolve app renderer from the SDK
reviewComment:
## REQUEST_CHANGES

The PR makes `generateEntry` emit an absolute, Node-resolved path to `react-dom/client` (resolved from the SDK's own dependency tree via `createRequire(import.meta.url)`) instead of the bare `react-dom/client` specifier, so apps under pnpm's strict layout no longer need to declare `react-dom` themselves. Four apps (browser-automation, system, dream, inbox) drop `react-dom`/`@types/react-dom`, the lockfile is regenerated, and the knip ratchet is lowered from 39 to 31 (8 findings, matching the issue). I verified the full `generateEntry.ts`, its single call site in `createRslibConfig.ts` (rspack `bundle: true`, `autoExternal: false`, so the absolute path is inlined), `build.ts`/`dev.ts`, the SDK runtime (no `react-dom` usage), and that none of the four apps depends on `@rome-os/ui` (whose peers still require `react-dom`). Within this repo the change is sound: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` overrides pin `react`/`react-dom` to 19.2.6 everywhere, so the SDK's react-dom and the app's react collapse to a single real path.

The design concern is what happens outside the monorepo, which is the SDK's primary audience (`@rome-os/app-web-sdk` is published and scaffolded apps consume it from npm). After this change the generated entry imports `react` from the app's tree and `react-dom` from the SDK's tree; pnpm satisfies react-dom's `react` peer from the SDK's own `react` dependency, not the app's. Nothing enforces that those two resolve to the same version, and if they diverge the bundle contains two React instances (hooks fail at runtime). Before the PR both resolved from the app root and were always consistent. A cheap fix exists (have the SDK own both and alias `react`/`react-dom`/`react/jsx-runtime` in the rslib config, or at least fail the build on a version mismatch). There is also no unit test for `generateEntry`, which now depends on the resolution environment.

**Verdict:** REQUEST_CHANGES — The manifest cleanup is correct, but the SDK change splits the React/ReactDOM pair across two resolution roots (app owns `react`, SDK owns `react-dom`), which is only safe inside this monorepo because of the workspace `overrides` pins — published-SDK consumers can end up with two React copies in one bundle.

### Findings (3)

- **[P1] react and react-dom now resolve from different roots — risk of two React instances for published-SDK consumers** (`packages/app-web-sdk/src/cli/generateEntry.ts:16` · architecture)
  After this change the generated entry pulls `react` from the app's `node_modules` (bare import, line 18) but `react-dom` from the SDK's tree. Under pnpm, react-dom's `react` peer is satisfied by the SDK's own `react` dependency, so the pair is only guaranteed to be one instance when the app's `react` and the SDK's `react` resolve to the same version. That holds here only because `pnpm-workspace.yaml` overrides pin `react`/`react-dom` to 19.2.6; an external app installing `@rome-os/app-web-sdk` from npm with e.g. `react: 19.1.0` pinned would bundle two Reacts and fail at runtime with "Invalid hook call". Before the PR both resolved from the app root, so the pair was always consistent. Suggest making the SDK the single owner of the pair: add `resolve.alias` for `react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `react/jsx-dev-runtime`, and `react-dom` in `createRslibConfig.ts` (using `dirname(require.resolve("<pkg>/package.json"))`), or at minimum compare `require('react/package.json').version` from the SDK against the one resolved from `appDir` and throw a clear build error on mismatch.

- **[P2] No test covers generateEntry, which now depends on the module-resolution environment** (`packages/app-web-sdk/src/cli/generateEntry.ts:12` · code-quality)
  `generateEntry` has no unit test (only `upgrade.test.ts` exists in `src/cli/`), and this PR makes its output depend on `createRequire(import.meta.url)` succeeding from wherever the compiled `dist/cli/generateEntry.js` lands. A small test that writes to a temp dir and asserts the emitted `react-dom/client` import is an absolute path ending in `react-dom/client.js` (and that the user-entry specifier is still relative) would catch regressions when the SDK's packaging or dependency layout changes (e.g. if `react-dom` is ever moved to peers, `require.resolve` will throw at build time for every app).

- **[P3] Prefer a bundler alias over baking a Node-resolved file path into generated source** (`packages/app-web-sdk/src/cli/generateEntry.ts:19` · design)
  `require.resolve` applies Node's `require`/`default` export conditions and returns a concrete file (`.../react-dom/client.js`), which the bundler then imports directly, bypassing react-dom's `exports` map and any `browser`/`module`/`import` conditions rspack would normally apply. It's benign for react-dom today, but it couples the SDK to react-dom's internal file layout and makes the generated `main.tsx` machine-specific. Putting the resolution in `createRslibConfig.ts` as `resolve.alias: { "react-dom": dirname(require.resolve("react-dom/package.json")) }` keeps the generated entry as `import ... from "react-dom/client"` and lets rspack resolve the subpath through the package's own `exports`.

## APPROVE

This PR removes four unused runtime dependencies (`@rome-os/app-runtime` from workflow-studio, `@radix-ui/react-dialog` and `tailwindcss` from connector, `uuid` from packages/web), keeps `expo-notifications` in packages/mobile with a documented Knip `ignoreDependencies` entry because `app.json` registers it as an Expo config plugin, and lowers the `lint:deadcode` `--max-issues` ratchet from 39 to 34. The lockfile changes are limited to importer removals and the resulting pnpm peer-suffix re-resolution on `@expo/*` / `@react-native/*` snapshots (no version bumps).

I verified each removal beyond the diff: workflow-studio has no server-side code and only imports `@rome-os/app-web-sdk` and `react`; the connector has zero references to either removed package and receives Tailwind through `@rome-os/app-web-sdk/styles` plus the SDK's `createRslibConfig.ts` PostCSS plugin (the same way `recap` and `showcases` already work); `packages/web` has no `uuid` import; and `packages/mobile` has no JS import of `expo-notifications` (the injectable `push-registration.ts` module is not yet wired into `App.tsx`, which is pre-existing and out of scope). The knip exception mirrors the existing `packages/desktop` precedent with a clear mechanism comment, and 4 removals + 1 exception = 5 matches the ratchet delta the issue requires. No bugs, security, or design concerns.

**Verdict:** APPROVE — All four dependency removals are verified unused in source and build pipelines, the expo-notifications exception is correctly justified and follows the existing knip.jsonc pattern, and the dead-code ratchet is lowered by exactly the number of resolved findings.
